[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like this, SPY and its analogs delivered a median 5-session return of -0.1%, with outcomes ranging from -5.12% to 6.88%. The single number to anchor on is that median: essentially flat, but sitting in a distribution where 52% of the paths finished below zero.

[state]
This state is defined by three features pulling hard in opposite directions. The 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) sits at -1.985, indicating unusually thin liquidity. At the same time, WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) is up 19.24%, a +1.124 standard deviation shock. Meanwhile, 20-session realised volatility (vol20) is compressed at 9.16%. The engine also notes the instrument is -2.27% from its 52-week high (dist52), with a 5d/20d volatility ratio (volRatio) of 1.192 and a mean absolute overnight gap (gap20) of 0.37%. These features pull recent broad ETF sessions—particularly from August and September 2026—into the neighborhood. Macro context shows VIX at 15.44, a 10y-2y Treasury slope of 0.25, and a 90-day Fed funds target change proxy of 0.25 bp. Market sentiment registers as Greed with a fearGreedValue of 70. Headlines framing the backdrop include CNBC Markets reporting "Stock futures are flat as investors grapple with higher yields, await Fed minutes" and "Surging Treasury yields don’t signal a U.S. 'fiscal apocalypse' — yet." Derivatives positioning data is unavailable on this card.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs, the mean 5-session return was -0.03% and the median was -0.1%, with a standard deviation of 2.14%. The distribution carries a slight positive skew of 0.51, meaning the upside tail stretched further than the downside: the maximum gain was 6.88% while the worst loss was -5.12%. The 10th percentile outcome was -2.39% and the 90th percentile was 3.29%. In 48% of the episodes the path finished above zero; in 52% it finished below. Only 2% of the analogs fell more than -5%, and none breached -10% or -20%. The bad tail is dominated by recent broad-market weakness. IWM on 2026-09-08 returned -2.98% with a max adverse excursion of -3.59%. JPM on 2026-09-04 returned -2.37% with a -3.09% adverse excursion. SPY itself on 2026-09-03 returned -1.15%, and DIA on 2026-09-02 returned -1.86%. Conversely, SPY on 2025-06-20 returned 3.47%, showing the upside dispersion available in this state.

[tails]
A trade can end near flat and still be un-holdable along the way. The median max adverse excursion across the 50 analogs was -1.05%. At the 25th percentile, the path dipped -1.98% intra-horizon, and at the 10th percentile it reached -3.1%. On the favourable side, the median max favourable excursion was 0.99%, reaching 1.89% at the 75th percentile and 3.52% at the 90th. The reward-to-risk ratio based on these excursions is 0.94. Looking at drawdown breaches during the 5-session window, 4% of the analog paths breached a -5% drawdown threshold. Zero percent breached -10%, -15%, or -20%.

[stress]
The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario produced a median forward return of -4.61%, which is -4.51% worse than the baseline median. The 10th percentile plunged to -11.63%, and 41.7% of those analogs breached a 10% drawdown. Caveat: Central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns. It is a sample of one regime, not a forecast of the next one. The 2025-04 tariff shock yielded a median of -0.92% (-0.82% versus baseline), but its 10th percentile hit -11.26% with a 23.1% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Caveat: Policy reversals inside the window make the tail of the distribution asymmetric in a way that is specific to that episode. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario showed a median of -2.09% (-1.99% versus baseline) and a 10th percentile of -5.01%. Caveat: A nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly; treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare delivered a median of -1.09% (-0.99% versus baseline). Caveat: Ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind had a median of -0.49% (-0.39% versus baseline). Caveat: Reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2023-03 regional bank stress actually improved the median to 1.41% (+1.51% versus baseline). Caveat: Very short window; the analog set will be dominated by a handful of sessions.
